history.period: 8th-9th century CE (some local sources say 11th century, but evidence points to 8th-9th)
history.summary: Oldest surviving religious monument inside Gwalior Fort, dated to the 8th-9th century CE (attributed by some to the Gurjara-Pratihara king Mihira Bhoja). It is an extraordinary North-South hybrid: a Nagara-style sandstone base with a towering ~100 ft barrel-vaulted (valabhi) Dravidian shikhara. Deity attribution is CONTESTED: a Shiva linga sits inside today and some sources call it a Shiva temple, while MP Tourism and others call it a Vishnu temple (a Garuda relief on the doorway supports the Vishnu reading). It suffered damage in the 1232 CE raids by Iltutmish's forces; the British later used the courtyard as a coffee shop/drinks factory, and the temple was restored in 1881-83 by Major Keith. Legend links the name 'Teli' (oilman) to oil-merchant patronage. It is a protected ASI monument with no regular worship, so no festival calendar.

name: Teli Ka Mandir
town_description: Gwalior is a historic city in northern Madhya Pradesh, dominated by the massive hilltop Gwalior Fort. Ruled by the Gurjara-Pratiharas, Kachchhapaghatas, Tomars, Mughals, Marathas and finally the Scindias, it is famed for its palaces, temples and Jain rock-cut sculptures. Gwalior is also a major centre of Hindustani classical music and the home of the Gwalior gharana.
tradition: Hinduism (sectarian attribution contested: Shaivism and Vaishnavism)
